quests.question: Her performance this quarter was _____ — she met all the basic expectations of the role.
quests.instruction: Select the word that best completes the sentence.
quests.hint: This word describes meeting standard expectations, neither praised strongly nor criticized.
quests.explanation: Satisfactory describes simply meeting expectations, matching 'met all the basic expectations.' Exemplary would suggest outstanding, model performance, far stronger praise than what a neutral, standard review calls for.

quests.question: Unfortunately, his attendance record has been _____, missing nearly a third of scheduled shifts.
quests.instruction: Select the word that best completes the sentence.
quests.hint: This word implies falling below an acceptable standard, signaling a problem needing correction.
quests.explanation: Subpar implies falling below an acceptable standard, matching 'unfortunately' and missing a third of shifts. Satisfactory would sound contradictory here, since the sentence is clearly flagging a serious performance problem.

quests.question: The team's handling of the crisis was truly _____, going above and beyond what anyone expected.
quests.instruction: Select the word that best completes the sentence.
quests.hint: This word implies outstanding, model performance worthy of being held up as an example.
quests.explanation: Exemplary implies outstanding, model performance, matching 'truly' and 'above and beyond what anyone expected.' Satisfactory would badly undersell a performance being praised as exceptional and worth celebrating.

quests.question: Your son seems to be _____ with the reading material — he's having trouble keeping up with the rest of the class.
quests.instruction: Select the word that best completes the sentence.
quests.hint: This diplomatic, general word describes having difficulty without assigning blame to the student.
quests.explanation: Struggling is a diplomatic, general word for having difficulty, common in parent-teacher conferences because it doesn't assign blame. Failing would sound harsher and more final, an unnecessarily severe word for this supportive conversation.

quests.question: With three tests and a project all due the same week, she's clearly _____ right now.
quests.instruction: Select the word that best completes the sentence.
quests.hint: This word implies too much demand relative to capacity at a specific moment, pointing to circumstances rather than ability.
quests.explanation: Overwhelmed points to circumstances, matching the pile-up of 'three tests and a project' due the same week. Struggling would suggest an ongoing difficulty with the material itself, rather than a temporary crunch caused by bad timing.

quests.question: He used to raise his hand constantly, but lately he seems completely _____ during class discussions.
quests.instruction: Select the word that best completes the sentence.
quests.hint: This word implies a lack of interest or participation, a shift in motivation rather than ability.
quests.explanation: Disengaged implies a shift in motivation and attention, matching the contrast with 'used to raise his hand constantly.' Struggling would suggest difficulty with the material, a different concern than a noticeable drop in participation.

quests.question: Attendance at the safety training session is _____ for all warehouse staff.
quests.instruction: Select the word that best completes the sentence.
quests.hint: This word implies a strict, non-negotiable requirement, the strongest directive strength.
quests.explanation: Mandatory implies a strict, non-negotiable requirement, standard in workplace safety policy. Recommended would suggest a strong but optional suggestion, which contradicts the firm, binding nature of a required safety session.

quests.question: While not required, a follow-up appointment is _____ within two weeks of the procedure.
quests.instruction: Select the word that best completes the sentence.
quests.hint: This word implies a strong expert suggestion that stops short of being a strict requirement.
quests.explanation: Recommended implies a strong expert suggestion, matching 'while not required' explicitly stated beforehand. Mandatory would directly contradict the sentence, which is clear that this appointment is advised rather than compulsory.

quests.question: Signing up for the newsletter is completely _____ — you can still access all the course materials without it.
quests.instruction: Select the word that best completes the sentence.
quests.hint: This word implies no obligation at all, purely a matter of personal choice, the weakest directive strength.
quests.explanation: Optional implies no obligation, matching 'you can still access all the course materials without it.' Recommended would suggest some encouragement to sign up, which understates just how freely skippable this newsletter really is.

quests.question: Smoking is strictly _____ within fifty feet of the building entrance.
quests.instruction: Select the word that best completes the sentence.
quests.hint: This word implies an absolute rule against something, the strongest level of restriction.
quests.explanation: Prohibited implies an absolute rule, matching 'strictly' and a firm, formal boundary near the entrance. Restricted would suggest limited access for some people, not a complete ban applying to everyone in the area.

quests.question: Access to the server room is _____ to employees with special security clearance.
quests.instruction: Select the word that best completes the sentence.
quests.hint: This word implies limited access to a specific group, rather than a blanket ban for everyone.
quests.explanation: Restricted implies limited access to a qualifying group, matching 'to employees with special security clearance.' Prohibited would suggest nobody can enter at all, which contradicts the cleared employees who clearly can.

quests.question: While not against the rules, bringing outside food into the theater is generally _____.
quests.instruction: Select the word that best completes the sentence.
quests.hint: This word implies a mild, soft suggestion against something, without it being an actual rule.
quests.explanation: Discouraged implies a soft suggestion rather than a rule, matching 'while not against the rules.' Prohibited would directly contradict the sentence, which explicitly states this behavior isn't actually forbidden.

quests.question: I think there's been a small _____ — I thought you meant Tuesday, not Thursday.
quests.instruction: Select the word that best completes the sentence.
quests.hint: This mild, diplomatic word implies an innocent mix-up rather than assigning fault to anyone.
quests.explanation: Misunderstanding is the mildest, most diplomatic word, implying an innocent mix-up over a date. Conflict would sound far too serious and confrontational for a small, easily resolved scheduling mix-up like this.

quests.question: The delayed shipment was caused by a _____ between the warehouse team and the shipping department about which order to prioritize.
quests.instruction: Select the word that best completes the sentence.
quests.hint: This word implies a breakdown in how information was exchanged between two teams or departments.
quests.explanation: Miscommunication implies a breakdown in how information moved between departments, matching a process-level explanation for the delay. Misunderstanding would sound more personal and individual, less suited to this systemic, business-process issue.

quests.question: The ongoing _____ between the two department heads has started to affect team morale.
quests.instruction: Select the word that best completes the sentence.
quests.hint: This stronger, more direct word signals a deeper, sustained interpersonal disagreement, not a simple mix-up.
quests.explanation: Conflict signals a deeper, sustained disagreement, matching 'ongoing' and its impact on 'team morale.' Misunderstanding would sound far too mild for a lasting interpersonal problem serious enough to affect an entire team.

quests.question: Her work quality has been _____ lately — sometimes excellent, sometimes full of careless errors.
quests.instruction: Select the word that best completes the sentence.
quests.hint: This relatively neutral, diagnostic word describes variable quality without a clear pattern.
quests.explanation: Inconsistent neutrally describes variable quality, matching 'sometimes excellent, sometimes full of errors.' Erratic would suggest more alarming, unpredictable swings, a stronger and less measured word than this diagnostic observation calls for.

quests.question: He's become so _____ that his team never knows if he'll show up to meetings on time or at all.
quests.instruction: Select the word that best completes the sentence.
quests.hint: This word implies a pattern of failing to be counted on, a stronger judgment specifically about dependability.
quests.explanation: Unreliable implies a pattern of failing to be counted on, matching 'never knows if he'll show up.' Inconsistent would describe variable quality of work, missing that specific, trust-related concern about dependability itself.

quests.question: His behavior in meetings has grown increasingly _____, swinging from calm to agitated without warning.
quests.instruction: Select the word that best completes the sentence.
quests.hint: This word implies unpredictable, sudden shifts, often carrying a concerning or unsettling connotation.
quests.explanation: Erratic implies sudden, unpredictable shifts, matching 'swinging from calm to agitated without warning.' Inconsistent would sound too mild and diagnostic for behavior that's actually alarming colleagues in meetings.

quests.question: Your daughter's grades have shown a _____ drop this semester, and we'd like to schedule a meeting to discuss it.
quests.instruction: Select the word that best completes the sentence.
quests.hint: This is the standard, measured word for a diplomatic professional communication that signals a problem without causing panic.
quests.explanation: Concerning is the standard, measured word for professional communication, signaling a problem calmly. Alarming would sound overly dramatic for a routine 'let's schedule a meeting' conversation, potentially causing unnecessary panic.

quests.question: The nurse noted some _____ changes in the patient's blood pressure that warranted a follow-up visit.
quests.instruction: Select the word that best completes the sentence.
quests.hint: This word implies genuine cause for attention, stronger than a routine note but still measured, not urgent.
quests.explanation: Worrisome implies genuine attention is warranted, matching 'warranted a follow-up visit' rather than immediate emergency care. Alarming would suggest urgent danger, too strong a word for a change that simply needs monitoring.

quests.question: Inspectors described the building's structural damage as _____, recommending immediate evacuation.
quests.instruction: Select the word that best completes the sentence.
quests.hint: This strongest word implies urgent danger requiring immediate action.
quests.explanation: Alarming implies urgent danger, matching 'recommending immediate evacuation.' Concerning would be far too mild a word for damage serious enough to require people to leave a building right away.

quests.question: There's been some _____ between the two new hires ever since they were assigned to the same project.
quests.instruction: Select the word that best completes the sentence.
quests.hint: This mild, common word implies a general sense of unease or strain, without open conflict.
quests.explanation: Tension is the mild, everyday word for a general sense of unease, fitting new coworkers still adjusting to each other. Hostility would suggest open antagonism, far too strong a word for this early, low-level awkwardness.

quests.question: The merger created noticeable _____ between employees from the two companies, who had very different work cultures.
quests.instruction: Select the word that best completes the sentence.
quests.hint: This word implies active, ongoing clashes arising from incompatible approaches, stronger than general unease.
quests.explanation: Friction implies active clashes from incompatible approaches, matching 'very different work cultures' colliding. Tension would suggest a vaguer, more passive unease, missing that sense of actual, ongoing disagreement over how things should work.

quests.question: By the end of the lawsuit, there was open _____ between the former business partners, who refused to even be in the same room.
quests.instruction: Select the word that best completes the sentence.
quests.hint: This strongest word implies open, active antagonism, not just strain or disagreement.
quests.explanation: Hostility implies open antagonism, matching 'refused to even be in the same room' after a lawsuit. Friction would suggest ongoing clashes but not necessarily the deep animosity described by two people avoiding each other entirely.

quests.question: As a _____, the city is asking residents near the river to keep sandbags ready in case of flooding.
quests.instruction: Select the word that best completes the sentence.
quests.hint: This mildest word implies a proactive protective step taken before any danger is confirmed.
quests.explanation: Precaution implies a proactive, protective step before danger is confirmed, matching 'in case of flooding.' Warning would suggest an active alert about a known, likely event, stronger than this forward-looking preventive request.

quests.question: The National Weather Service issued a _____ for severe thunderstorms expected to hit the area tonight.
quests.instruction: Select the word that best completes the sentence.
quests.hint: This standard word implies an official alert about a known or expected danger.
quests.explanation: Warning is the standard term for an official alert about expected danger, matching 'expected to hit the area tonight.' Precaution would suggest a preventive step rather than the alert itself being issued by weather officials.

quests.question: The hacker group posted an online _____ claiming they would release the stolen data unless the ransom was paid.
quests.instruction: Select the word that best completes the sentence.
quests.hint: This strongest word implies an explicit, directed statement of intent to cause harm.
quests.explanation: Threat implies a directed, intentional statement of harm, matching 'unless the ransom was paid.' Warning would suggest an informational alert about danger, missing that deliberate, menacing intent behind the hackers' demand.

quests.question: Wearing jeans to the office is _____ on Fridays, but not during the rest of the week.
quests.instruction: Select the word that best completes the sentence.
quests.hint: This word implies meeting the minimum standard of what's allowed, not necessarily preferred.
quests.explanation: Acceptable implies meeting the minimum standard of what's permitted, matching a specific, limited exception on Fridays. Ideal would suggest the best possible choice, too strong a word for something that's merely tolerated one day a week.

quests.question: A firm handshake and direct eye contact are considered _____ during a job interview in most Western business cultures.
quests.instruction: Select the word that best completes the sentence.
quests.hint: This word implies fitting well with a specific context or cultural norm.
quests.explanation: Appropriate implies fitting well with a specific cultural context, matching 'in most Western business cultures.' Acceptable would suggest merely being allowed, missing that stronger sense of precisely matching expected norms.

quests.question: The _____ candidate for this role would have both technical expertise and strong communication skills, though we know such a perfect match is rare.
quests.instruction: Select the word that best completes the sentence.
quests.hint: This word implies the best possible option, a standard to aspire to rather than simply what's allowed.
quests.explanation: Ideal implies the best possible option, matching 'though we know such a perfect match is rare.' Acceptable would describe the minimum standard, the opposite of the aspirational, hard-to-find combination being described here.
